whyThisShow: This show is remembered as much for what happened offstage as on. An eyewitness account describes Jerry and Bobby in a visible confrontation in the wings after the Lost Sailor → Saint of Circumstance, with one attendee recalling "Jerry lit into him. I thought for a second it was gonna come to blows. I think it was Steve Parrish who intervened" [source: 'Jerry lit into him. I thought for a second it was gonna come to blows. I think it was Steve Parrish who intervened.']. Whatever the source of the friction, the show delivered: one reviewer notes this was "the last Sailor/Saint with Garcia" [source: 'this was the last Sailor/Saint with Garcia'], which gives the entire sequence an unplanned weight in retrospect. One attendee noted the show started out with "Jerry Playing Better Than The Earlier Shows Of The Tour" [source: 'The Show Started Out Hot With Jerry Playing Better Than The Earlier Shows Of The Tour']. The Help→Slipknot!→Franklin's Tower and the reportedly charged Morning Dew round out a night the community treats as a classic, even without an official release.
listenFor: The Lost Sailor → Saint of Circumstance is the centerpiece listen here — one attendee who was standing near the stage urged listeners to "Listen For The Feedback Growl From Jerry Seconds Into It" [source: 'Listen For The Feedback Growl From Jerry Seconds Into It']. After Space, the band returned for just a single song before the encore, which one listener flagged as almost certainly unique: "I'm pretty sure this is the only time that happened in this show format" [source: "I'm pretty sure this is the only time that happened in this show format"]. The Morning Dew that followed the backstage confrontation is described as "a Furious Dew" [source: 'a Furious Dew Insued'], so treat that as required listening. One reviewer also singles out Phil's vocal on Box of Rain, writing that he thinks Phil sung it better in 86 than in later years [source: 'I think Phil sung "Box of Rain" Better in '86 than '87-'95']. Be aware that the SBD on Archive has patches: "part of El Paso, all of Drums, and all of the Dew are all an audience patch" [source: 'part of El Paso,all of Drums, and all of the Dew are all an audience patch'], so some listeners recommend hunting down the audience recording instead.
context: This is a March 1986 show at The Spectrum in Philadelphia, part of a spring tour. The recording on Archive (gd86-03-24.sbd.miller.22783.sbeok.shnf) is a soundboard but contains known patches sourced from an audience tape for portions of the second set. The show has never received an official release. One attendee described attending the first six shows of this tour as a honeymoon trip, noting it led to "31 Years And Counting Of Blessed Partnership And Love" [source: 'A Honeymoon Excursion That Led To 31 Years And Counting Of Blessed Partnership And Love'].
funFact: After the backstage confrontation, one eyewitness reported that "Jerry Came Back Out And Sat Alone In A Little Aclove Of Speakers And Amps Hidden From Sight" before Steve Parrish came out and talked him back onstage [source: 'Jerry Came Back Out And Sat Alone In A Little Aclove Of Speakers And Amps Hidden From Sight. Steve Came Out After A While Leaned Over And Said Something To Jerry Who Furiously Chain Smokin Appeared Very Animated'].
headline: Philly '86 — the last Sailor/Saint, and a backstage blowup.
